# fixtures

The fixtures are hand-authored minimal MusicXML. Every expected output was derived by hand from the
writing rules in `../../CLAUDE.md`; none was generated by running the app. Unless noted otherwise,
each score has two parts: *Trombone* (`<midi-program>58`) and *Tuba* (`<midi-program>59`).
Rehearsal marks sit on the Trombone part only, as MuseScore writes them. All are 4/4 with
`<divisions>1`.

Notes are written as `F2` (step, accidental, octave). `×2` means the measures are written out twice.

| input | concern | tuba part, measure by measure |
|---|---|---|
| `cycle_single_note` | rule 3: a one-measure cycle is written four times | Bb2 Bb2 Bb2 Bb2, six measures |
| `cycle_four_measures` | rule 2 cycle; rule 1 collapse inside a measure; a ↓ arrow | (F2 F2 F2 F2 \| Ab2 \| Db2 Eb2 \| F2) ×2 |
| `cycle_with_folding` | rule 4: a group inside a cycle | ((Ab2 G2 \| F2) ×3, Bb2 Eb2 \| F2) ×2 |
| `whole_line` | no cycle, so the whole line; a repeated single measure is not folded | Bb2 \| A2 \| D2 \| D2 \| F2 G2 \| A2 |
| `whole_line_with_folding` | a group inside a whole line; group entry and exit; an apostrophe in the title | Bb2 \| A2 \| D2 \| F2 \| D2 \| F2 \| G2 |
| `ties_rests_chords` | rule 1: rests, a tie across the barline, a rest-only measure, a chord (lowest note; written high note first), a grace note, repeated pitches | rest F2 G2~ \| ~G2 A2 \| rest \| {E3,C3} grace D3, Bb2 \| F2 F2 rest |
| `repeats_and_voltas` | repeats and voltas are expanded before writing | \|: F2 \| Ab2 \| [1. Db2 Eb2 :\|] [2. C2] |
| `medley_two_songs` | song split: two marks, a gap measure with tempo + key change, the same mark repeated (continuation), a trailing gap | C3 ×3 \| gap \| Bb2 Ab2 \| Eb3 \| (mark again) Bb2 Ab2 \| Eb3 \| gap |
| `leading_untitled` | notes before the first mark form a song titled from `<work-title>` | Bb2 \| Bb2 \| (mark) F2 G2 \| Ab2 \| F2 G2 \| Ab2 |
| `no_rehearsal_mark` | no marks: one song titled from `<work-title>`; the old hand-written `C↑` becomes `C` | (F2 \| Ab2 \| C3 \| C3) ×2 |
| `rest_closes_repeat` | song split: a rest-only measure that carries the closing repeat sign is part of the song, not a gap; the gap after it is trimmed | \|: F2 \| Ab2 \| rest :\| ; gap ; Bb2 \| A2 \| D2 |
| `tuba_by_midi_program` | tuba detected by `<midi-program>59` on a part named "Baixo" | F2 \| A2 \| D3 \| Bb2 |
| `no_tuba_part` | Trombone only: an empty tuba line (and warning E07 in the view tests) | none |
| `broken_xml` | truncated file → E05 | — |
| `empty_score` | rests only → E06 | — |
| `project_file.mscz` | MuseScore project file → E02 | — |

`output/*.csv` files are UTF-8 **without** the BOM and use LF; compare them after normalising line
endings and decoding the export with `utf-8-sig`.

## scenarios/reorder

The scenario loads `medley_two_songs`, `tuba_by_midi_program` and `no_tuba_part` and exports the set
list in `order.txt`. It checks three things:

- songs are ordered **across** files;
- the "Baixo" tuba and the "Tuba" tuba land in one canonical Tuba part, so both lines survive the
  re-import;
- a song whose score had no tuba part gets rests there and comes back with an empty line.
